chain.label: ValuJet work card 0069 lacked disposal instructions and inspector signoff
chain.trigger: work card 0069 does not contain the eighth step listed in the Douglas MD-80 maintenance manual, "Store or dispose of oxygen generator"... work card 0069 did not require an inspector's signature

chain.label: Removed generators carried no hazardous materials label or warning marking
chain.trigger: The expired generators did not have labels or markings on them warning of the high temperatures generated during activation, or any emblems indicating that the generators were a hazardous material

chain.label: Class D forward cargo compartment had no smoke detection or fire suppression
chain.trigger: the cargo compartment where the fire occurred was a class D cargo compartment and was not equipped... with a smoke detection system... nor a fire suppression system

chain.label: FAA failed to require detection/suppression in class D compartments despite prior recommendations
chain.trigger: had the FAA required fire/smoke detection and fire extinguishment systems in class D cargo compartments, as the Safety Board recommended in 1988, ValuJet flight 592 would likely not have crashed

caused_by.evidence: the FAA responded... stating that fire/smoke detection and fire extinguishment systems were not cost beneficial... and that it had terminated its rulemaking action

chain.label: SabreTech and ValuJet personnel untrained in hazmat handling and ValuJet's no-carry policy
chain.trigger: the SabreTech Miami facility did not provide a hazardous materials training program to its employees regarding the recognition or shipping of hazardous materials, nor was such a program provided by ValuJet

caused_by.evidence: ValuJet's failure to ensure that both ValuJet and contract maintenance facility employees were aware of the carrier's "no-carry" hazardous materials policy and had received appropriate hazardous materials training

chain.label: SabreTech mechanics removed generators without installing safety caps
chain.trigger: safety caps were not installed over the percussion caps that start a chemical reaction in the oxygen generators

caused_by.evidence: had work card 0069 required an inspector's signoff, one of the inspectors... might have noticed that safety caps had not been installed
the supervisor told him that the company did not have any safety caps available

chain.label: Mechanics and inspectors signed off work card 0069 knowing caps were not installed
chain.trigger: the SabreTech inspector who signed off the "Final Inspection" block... said that at the time he signed off he was aware that the generators needed safety caps

caused_by.evidence: When asked if he had followed up to see if safety caps had been put on the generators before the time he signed off the card, he said that he had not

chain.label: ValuJet failed to oversee SabreTech's handling of the generators
chain.trigger: the failure of ValuJet to properly oversee its contract maintenance program to ensure compliance with maintenance, maintenance training, and hazardous materials requirements and practices

caused_by.evidence: ValuJet failed to provide significant on-site quality assurance at SabreTech's Miami facility... failed to discover the improper maintenance signoffs indicating that safety caps had been installed

chain.label: FAA failed to adequately monitor ValuJet's heavy maintenance and prior generator fires
chain.trigger: the failure of the FAA to adequately monitor ValuJet's heavy maintenance programs and responsibilities, including ValuJet's oversight of its contractors

caused_by.evidence: before the accident, the FAA's oversight of ValuJet did not include any significant oversight of its heavy maintenance functions

chain.label: Stock clerk repacked uncapped generators and labeled the shipment "Oxy Cannisters-Empty"
chain.trigger: he identified the generators as "empty canisters" because none of the mechanics had talked with him about what they were... when he saw that they had green tags on them, he assumed that meant they were empty

caused_by.evidence: None of the SabreTech mechanics remembered seeing any type of hazardous materials warning label on any of the boxes that contained the old generators
he did not have any training specific to the air shipment of hazardous materials
He stated that he did not put caps on the generators but placed the generators into the same cardboard tubes

chain.label: ValuJet ramp agents accepted and loaded the undeclared hazardous shipment atop the tires
chain.trigger: the boxes... had no hazardous material markings or labels, and... the shipping ticket... indicated that the boxes contained empty oxygen canisters

caused_by.evidence: neither the ValuJet lead ramp agent nor the ramp agent who loaded the boxes were provided with information to indicate the hazardous nature of the COMAT shipment

chain.label: One or more oxygen generators actuated in the forward cargo compartment
chain.trigger: the activation of one or more chemical oxygen generators in the forward cargo compartment of the airplane initiated the fire on ValuJet flight 592

caused_by.evidence: it is very likely that had safety caps been installed, the generators would not have activated and the accident would not have occurred
the generators were not packaged adequately to prevent generators from striking the actuation mechanism or dislodging retaining pins on adjacent generators

chain.label: Intense oxygen-fed fire developed and breached the cargo compartment
chain.trigger: the oxygen generators would have initially fed the fire with an abundance of oxygen... resulting in a very rapidly developing fire

caused_by.evidence: Auto-ignition of the bubble wrap in contact with the hot surface of the generators in the presence of elevated concentrations of oxygen was the source of the ignition
the cockpit crew had no means available to extinguish or even suppress the fire in the cargo compartment

chain.label: Crew received no warning until smoke and fire reached the cabin about 6 minutes after takeoff
chain.trigger: the cockpit crew of ValuJet flight 592 had no way of detecting the threat to the safety of the airplane from the in-flight fire until smoke and fumes reached the passenger cabin

caused_by.evidence: a smoke/fire warning device would have more quickly alerted the pilots to the fire and would have allowed them more time to land the airplane
At 1410:27, the CVR recorded a male voice saying, "We're on fire, we're on fire."

chain.label: Crew turned back toward Miami accepting wide ATC vectors rather than immediate landing
chain.trigger: for the next 80 seconds the airplane continued on a northwesterly heading (away from the Miami airport) while the flightcrew accepted ATC vectors for a wide circle to the left

caused_by.evidence: The captain stated, "We need, we need to go back to Miami"

chain.label: Fire destroyed floor beams and flight control cables, progressively degrading control
chain.trigger: examination of the wreckage showed that before the impact the left side floor beams melted and collapsed, which would likely have affected the control cables on the captain's side

caused_by.evidence: The flight experienced a progressive degradation in the airplane's structural integrity and flight controls
the airplane remained under at least partial control by the flightcrew for about 3 minutes and 9 seconds

chain.label: Airplane rolled abruptly right and pitched nose down in an uncontrolled descent
chain.trigger: the loss of control was most likely the result of flight control failure from the extreme heat and structural collapse

caused_by.evidence: the airplane would have had to start rolling to the right at 1413:34, at least 8 seconds before the crash

chain.label: Airplane crashed into the Everglades at over 400 KIAS
chain.trigger: Ground scars and wreckage scatter indicate the airplane crashed into the Everglades in a right wing down, nose down attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airspeed of flight 592 was more than 400 KIAS and increasing at the time of ground impact

chain.label: All 110 occupants killed; accident not survivable
chain.trigger: Both pilots, the three flight attendants, and all 105 passengers were killed

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable
